scope: Three GitHub-hosted Ubuntu jobs, each four fresh ClickHouse servers in LC/RAW/RAW/LC order, all same compiled stock O1, source and fixture, no C++ modification. Replicated process CPU benefit, NOT production speed claim.
math_bound: For each runner r, compare the raw UUID mean across B1/B2 to the LC mean across A0/A3; do not pool absolute CPU seconds across different machines. A/A LC drift bound 25%, each per-runner CPU effect must exceed max(5%, local A/A drift) and have the same sign. Compare source input SHA, executable SHA manifest and native output before considering performance. Three runner jobs can reproduce a lab effect but cannot establish a statistical production hardware gain.

reducer.note: CI reducer validated three ZIP content manifests and hashes of locally repacked archives; official artifact digest PINs checked separately via GitHub API.

limitations: Three jobs still only one synthetic 400-node-independent fixture and same class of hosted runners. Not a general production statistical guarantee.
Absolute CPU values varied strongly across GitHub hosts; ratios were therefore computed within each runner, never pooled as raw timings.
Ingest wall benefit was inconsistent: one runner ~0.09% improvement despite lower CPU; do not promise write latency improvement.
Natural background merges and simultaneous native reads were disabled/absent during write stage; p95 Grafana latency and total system cost not measured.
No production-optimized jemalloc ClickHouse benchmark; do not extrapolate from -O1 glibc or assume config equivalence.
Read/DDL behavior limited to finite gauges and one grouping; no NaN/counters/ACL/multi-tenant security tests.

next_action.step: Run independent same-runner ABBA of continuous insert with natural merges enabled while one fixed native PromQL reader runs against an immutable 12-batch prefix; compare p95/p99 latency and whole-process CPU with exact oracle and valid A/A drift. Do not conflate those mixed results with write-only CI. Production allocator gate remains open.
next_action.stop_condition: Abort promotion on any native mismatch, OOM, unbounded background-merge backlog, profiler perturbation or A/A drift >25%; keep negative evidence.
